title: QUIC xquic Non-Handshake Residual Trace Architecture
purpose: Define the trace boundary for the remaining xquic client-role non-handshake liveness residual before transport changes are promoted.
design_summary: The remaining all-upstream client-role non-handshake gap is narrowed to xquic after the generic ordered-read wake-up, delayed-ACK threshold re-arm, quic-go transfer, quic-go chacha20, and quic-go keyupdate evidence were closed separately. This architecture keeps that residual as an evidence-owned investigation surface until focused packet, ingress, path, or stream proof identifies a concrete runtime change. The May 23 captured-packet proofs show the managed client emitted a decryptable post-burst ACK for xquic response packet 17 and then emitted repeated MAX_DATA/MAX_STREAM_DATA updates with increasing limits through packet 28, while the fresh May 23 live rerun reached `xqc_process_read_streams|stream_read_notify|flag:66` after the request stream was fully received and the response burst ran through packet 22 before `xqc_send_packet_pacer_allows|pacing blocked` at `stream_offset:16536` prevented the transfer from draining to FIN, so the next runtime investigation should prioritize post-send drain, pacing wakeup, peer delivery, xquic event-loop packet consumption, and stream-drain behavior before changing ACK generation, packet protection, or local credit publication. The local interop-runner helper now appends that narrowed shape and the xquic server-log short-header packet-processing ceiling through packets 0..3 as a non-promoting failure diagnostic when preserved xquic logs show only early ACK processing plus a managed client timeout. The trace boundary deliberately separates the mostly green all-upstream matrix from support readiness, does not imply HTTP/3 or broader API support, and avoids changing the inventory classifier until a dedicated xquic proof slice passes.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The xquic residual must stay separate from `REQ-QUIC-INT-0023`, which owns the already-closed quic-go download-liveness slice.
The all-upstream handshake profile under `REQ-QUIC-INT-0027` remains handshake-only and advisory.
The helper inventory under `REQ-QUIC-INT-0018` must not classify xquic-specific non-handshake residuals as support-readiness proof.
A later runtime fix needs focused positive and negative proof before the gap ledger can close this residual.

The captured ACK and credit-burst proofs narrow the current evidence away from missing client ACK emission or missing local credit publication but do not prove the xquic server consumed those later packets.

The runner diagnostic is classification-only: it keeps the run failed, may report the largest client short-header packet processed by xquic, and must not promote xquic support or suppress the need for later runtime proof.
risks: Treating xquic as a generic stream-read or ACK-cadence failure would reopen already-closed work and obscure the current narrowed evidence.
Promoting support from a mostly green all-upstream sweep would overstate the current implementation boundary.
